minutes.headline: Select Board heard two hours of anger over steep lakefront tax assessments and promised to investigate; assessor to attend next week.
minutes.summary: Most of the meeting was extended public comment on sharp FY2023 assessment and tax increases for Hickory Hills, Lake Shirley and Whalom properties. The board said the Board of Assessors controls assessments, but pledged to investigate, to meet with the principal assessor next week, and to look at abatement funding. Three people were appointed to the 300th Anniversary Committee by roll call, and the meeting adjourned.

what_happened.line: The Select Board spent most of the meeting on public comment about sharp FY2023 assessment and tax increases on Hickory Hills, Lake Shirley and Whalom properties.
The board said the Board of Assessors sets assessments, but promised to investigate and to meet with the principal assessor at next week's meeting, with time for questions.
Residents asked the board to raise abatement funding through line item transfers or free cash, and the vice chair said abatements should not be partial for lack of overlay money.
The chair said a town meeting before May to reallocate funds will be called if needed.
Three people were appointed to the 300th Anniversary Committee by roll call, and the meeting then adjourned.

why_it_matters: Residents with lakefront or other affected property may see a changed tax bill and may need to file for an abatement, a process whose timing and funding were questioned at this meeting.
If the abatement reserve (the overlay) is too small for the number of claims, the town could be asked to vote at a special town meeting to move money into it.
watch_next: Next week's Select Board meeting, when the principal assessor is to attend and take questions on the assessments.
A possible special town meeting before May to reallocate funds for abatements, if the board calls one.
